title: Freya and the Ember
premise: Juniper Lockridge, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons survived, secretly keeps accounts for the Ember Guild—a network that smuggles out people the usurper's regime has erased from existence. When a dying courier presses them a map of Vessany, a country annexed and struck from all records twenty years ago, Juniper learns the guild's founder came from there—and that the map opens the last door between the free cities and the armies hunting refugees through them. Pursued by an inquisitor who was once Juniper's childhood friend, they gather a found family of the unrecorded and uncounted to reopen the door. In the end, Juniper chooses to be counted: they testify before the free cities' council as a citizen of nowhere, the door opens not to escape but to sanctuary, and the inquisitor must decide whether ledgers or loyalty define her.
about_author: Paloma Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents belonging to people no one claimed. She writes fantasy about paperwork, poison, and the stubborn arithmetic of belonging.

chapters.title: A Taste for Bitterness
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. We meet them mid-service at the usurper's court, tasting a dish laced with something new, while mentally balancing the Ember Guild's hidden ledgers at night. Establishes their double life, their trained invisibility, and the quiet pride of keeping impossible accounts. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness—the comfort and cost of being no one.

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Delivery
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses in the guild's back room and presses a scorched map into Juniper's hands, whispering a word: Vessany. The guild's elders refuse it—too dangerous, too old—but Juniper recognizes the founder's handwriting from the earliest ledgers. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance; curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Won't Say
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with interludes from the guild matriarch Odile. Digging into twenty-year-old accounts, Juniper finds payments to a door-keeper in a country that officially never existed—and discovers the founder was Vessani. Meanwhile the court announces a census meant to flush out the unrecorded. Emotional beat: the past is not dead; it's itemized.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Welcome
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sable Vane's POV. Sable, tasked with the census, recognizes Juniper at court—the friend who vanished from her childhood village after a fire. She requests Juniper assigned as her taster on a progress through the free cities. Emotional beat: recognition as threat; old affection sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: Road Salt and Riddles
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the road, Juniper uses tasting duties as cover to contact Ember safehouses, gathering a ragtag company: Odile's runaway apprentice, a deaf cartographer, a deserter cook. The map reacts to one of them—the cartographer's Vessani blood. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself out of the counted-out.

chapters.title: The Census Rolls Through
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable conducts the census in a river town and finds names that shouldn't exist—Vessani ones. She begins connecting the Ember Guild to the map, and her doubt curdles into resolve when her superiors burn a family rather than record them. Emotional beat: the first crack in her faith in the ledger-state.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the map's final coordinates, the company finds not a door but a ruin—and an ambush by the usurper's vanguard, already marching on the free cities. Odile arrives with the truth: the door opens only for someone willing to be named. Emotional beat: betrayal of expectations; the cost of staying invisible made literal.

chapters.title: Named and Numbered
chapters.summary: Alternating Juniper and Sable POVs. Sable captures Juniper; in interrogation, instead of breaking them, she reads the confiscated ledgers and sees the arithmetic of mercy in every entry. Juniper offers her the choice she can't unmake: help open the door or watch the free cities fall. Emotional beat: confrontation as mirror; identity chosen over identity assigned.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vessany
chapters.summary: Full-company POV rotation. Climax: as the vanguard breaches the city walls, Juniper publicly declares themselves a citizen of Vessany before the free cities' council, giving the map a name to answer to. Sable turns her troops' route away from the refugee quarter. The door opens—not to a lost country, but to sanctuary for everyone the ledgers erased. Emotional beat: courage as testimony.

chapters.title: A New Set of Books
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue-like. The guild reorganizes around the open door; Juniper becomes its keeper of names, recording the previously unrecorded. Sable, stripped of rank, asks for a place among them. The last entry Juniper writes is their own name, spelled in full. Emotional beat: resolution as belonging—justice kept like accounts, honestly.
